newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees worst-case 8.5 pct inflation avg in 97.
newsitem.headline: Manila sees worst-case 8.5 pct inflation avg in 97.

text.p: The Philippine central bank has projected a worst-case scenario of 8.5 percent average inflation this year after a de facto devaluation of the peso last Friday, bank governor Gabriel Singson told reporters on Wednesday.
The government had earlier projected inflation might reach 5.2 to 5.7 percent this year.
Singson remained confident the inflation rate would not reach double-digits this year.
Assuming depreciation of three pesos against the dollar, Singson said inflation would average 7.5 percent in the third quarter of the year.
Consumer inflation averaged 4.6 percent in the first half of the year.
President Fidel Ramos earlier said prices of basic commodities have not risen after the peso plunged to a 45-month low of 30 pesos on Tuesday.
The peso was hovering at 26.40 to the dollar before the Central Bank announced it was letting the peso trade in a new, wider range.
Late on Wednesday, the currency was trading around 29.3 to the dollar.
